title: New York Times might buy Letterboxd for $330M US: report
summary: The ​New York Times Company is in exclusive talks to acquire film-focused social platform Letterboxd in a deal valued at about $330 million US, the New York Times reported on Thursday, citing two…

image.caption: The Letterboxd logo is seen on a smartphone. (Sebastian Gollnow/Getty Images)

blocks.text: The ​New York Times Company is in exclusive talks to acquire film-focused social platform Letterboxd in a deal valued at about $330 million US, the New York Times reported on Thursday, citing two ‌people familiar with the discussions.
No agreement has been reached and ​talks could still fall apart, says New York Times report
A deal would extend the media organization's push beyond its core news business, following acquisitions including sports site The Athletic, product-review service Wirecutter and the ​Wordle game.
The company added 420,000 digital-only ​subscribers in the third quarter, bringing total paid subscribers to 13.8 million.

No agreement has been reached and the ​talks could still fall apart, the report said. The price ⁠under consideration would value ⁠Letterboxd at more than 20 ‌times its projected earnings this year of about $15 million US, according to the newspaper.
The New York Times Company declined to comment, while Letterboxd did not immediately respond to a request ⁠for comment outside regular business hours.
Launched in 2011 by Matthew Buchanan and Karl von Randow, Letterboxd has grown rapidly since 2020, reaching 30 million users, ‌and is particularly popular among Gen Z film fans.
The Times Company and Letterboxd have ​discussed keeping Buchanan and von Randow in charge of the business, with the founders reporting ⁠to a Times Company executive, the report said.

Letterboxd's parent has been ⁠working with investment bank LionTree on a potential sale, the report ⁠said. ⁠Film studios A24 and Sony ​had been among prospective buyers, but A24 later dropped out as price expectations ​increased, the report ⁠said.

The New York Times Company would integrate its advertising technology with Letterboxd's systems, according to the report, which added that the film platform would likely continue operating as a standalone site for the foreseeable future.
